Xu and Xu cite Marx on the "natural historical process" and Xunzi on constancy and adaptation, and set the maxims "success need not be mine" and "success must include me" side by side. In the third, standing with human progress is described as a "critical construction" that rejects hegemonic systems and linear narratives of progress. The authors claim that a community with a shared future for mankind goes beyond realism, the "end of history" thesis and the "clash of civilizations" thesis, and they describe the Belt and Road Initiative as reshaping the logic of global spatial production. The authors conclude that historical resolve, in its global form, is a "civilizational resolve" that "creates within tension", and that the Party stands on the side of "time" and "momentum". They present Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation as a model of resolve guiding historical continuity through patience. Read the original if you want to see how Party-affiliated scholars give a Marxist philosophical grounding to a new official concept and tie it to Xi Jinping's formulations on history.

Resolutely block any attempt to revive Japanese militarism Interview with Hu Dekun, senior professor of humanities and social sciences at Wuhan University 坚决阻击任何妄想复活日本军国主义的图谋——访武汉大学人文社会科学资深教授胡德坤 Zhou Xiaofei This is an interview in Guangming Daily in which reporter Zhou Xiaofei questions Hu Dekun, a senior professor at Wuhan University, about remarks on Taiwan by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae. The interview presents the remarks as a sign that Japanese militarism has not disappeared. Hu argues that they echo a long tradition of aggression and breach the postwar international legal order. The interview has five questions. They cover the historical roots of the remarks, earlier cases where Japan invoked a "survival crisis" to justify war, the suffering caused by Japanese aggression, the international and bilateral legal documents Takaichi's words allegedly violate, and the measures the international community should take. Hu traces Japanese militarist thought from Toyotomi Hideyoshi's plans against Korea and China, through Tokugawa-era scholars and Yoshida Shōin, to the Meiji state's expansion. In his account, the Allied Tokyo Trial and the American occupation reforms removed its basis, but Cold War "support" for Japan let right-wing revisionism survive. He gives the Mukden Incident, the Marco Polo Bridge Incident and Pearl Harbor as cases of "survival crisis" and "self-defence" pretexts. Upholding the organic unity of law-based governance of the country and rule-based governance of the Party 坚持依法治国和依规治党有机统一 Ma Huaide Writing in the People's Daily on 12 January 2026, Ma Huaide takes up the principle, listed as the twelfth of the "twelve upholds" in the 2025 edition of the Study Outline on Xi Jinping Thought on the Rule of Law, that governing the country by law and governing the Party by its own rules must form an organic unity. Distilling signature concepts is a key dimension of building a body of sociological knowledge 提炼标识性概念是构建社会学知识体系的关键维度 Li Lingjing Li Lingjing, writing in Guangming Daily in January 2026, asks how Chinese sociology can build its own body of knowledge. The scientific connotation of high-efficacy governance and paths to advance it 高效能治理的科学内涵与推进路径 Mao Peijin Mao Peijin takes up the concept of high-efficacy governance (高效能治理), which Xi Jinping stressed in April and May 2025 in connection with planning for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Understanding and grasping "strengthening the Party's political leadership capacity" 深刻理解和把握“增强党的政治领导力” Huang Gang This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 8 January 2026, explains one phrase from the Central Committee's Recommendations for the 15th Five-Year Plan: strengthening the Party's "political leadership capacity". Raising quality and expanding capacity: strategic priorities for higher education in the 15th Five-Year Plan period 提质扩容：“十五五”时期高等教育战略重点 Li Liguo Writing in Guangming Daily (6 January 2026), Li Liguo takes up a line from the proposals adopted by the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan: promote "raising quality and expanding capacity" (tízhì kuòróng) in higher education and enlarge enrolment in high-quality undergraduate programmes. The three inherent determinations of Chinese modernization 中国式现代化的三重内在规定性 Zhao Jianying Zhao Jianying asks what makes Chinese modernization qualitatively different from Western modernization. The growth of Japanese militarism as a serious threat to the postwar international order Interview with Zhang Haipeng, Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences 日本军国主义滋长是对战后国际秩序的严重威胁——访中国社会科学院学部委员张海鹏 Zhao Fan This is an interview, published in Guangming Daily on 5 January 2026, in which reporter Zhao Fan questions the historian Zhang Haipeng, an Academic Member of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Understanding the operating mechanisms and key advantages of China's Five-Year Plans 深刻理解我国五年规划的作用机制和重要优势 Yang Yongheng Yang Yongheng, writing in People's Daily on the eve of the 15th Five-Year Plan period, asks how China's Five-Year Plans actually work and why they count as an institutional strength of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Carrying the Party's leadership through every aspect and the whole process of economic and social development 把党的领导贯穿经济社会发展各方面全过程 He Yiting Writing in the People's Daily on 7 January 2026, He Yiting takes up the Party's leadership as the first principle in the Recommendations of the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Further improving ideological guidance and cohesion services for new forms of employment groups 进一步做好新就业群体思想引导和凝聚服务工作 National Association for Party-Building Research (Quanguo Dangjian Yanjiuhui) This commentary, published in the People's Daily on 8 January 2026 under the name of the National Association for Party-Building Research, asks how the Party should guide and serve the "new employment groups" (platform-based and flexible workers such as couriers and delivery riders). Understanding the global significance of China's path, China's governance and China's principles 深刻把握中国之路中国之治中国之理的世界意义 Liu Haixing Writing in the People's Daily on 8 January 2026, Liu Haixing, identified as head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee, takes up the Proposals adopted at the Fourth Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2025) for the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Combining scientific achievements with dialectical thought: Engels's Dialectics of Nature at one hundred A retrospective and outlook 科技成果与辩证法思想结合——恩格斯《自然辩证法》出版百年的回顾与展望 Liu Dachun Marking a century since the first full publication of Engels's Dialectics of Nature in 1925, Liu Dachun asks what this unfinished manuscript still offers. Liu argues that, although incomplete, it shows Engels's insight into the laws of nature and of the natural sciences and his aim of joining scientific results to dialectical thought. In Liu's account, its study keeps generating new vitality and remains a source for views of nature, science and technology, and scientific method. The commentary has three parts. The first tells how the manuscript was written between 1873 and 1883, interrupted twice (by Anti-Dühring and by the editing of Capital), withheld by the Second International and finally published in Moscow under David Riazanov. Liu lists five ways it stays alive: John Bellamy Foster's reading of Engels as a founder of ecology and of the metabolic cycle; Stephen Jay Gould's link between labour in the transition from ape to human and gene–culture coevolution; Western workshops on a "digital dialectics of nature" applying Engels's laws to deep learning and AI explainability; Prigogine and Stengers's use of dialectical models in complexity science; and its role as a base for the interdisciplinary field of science, technology and society. Liu then names four contemporary values: refining the Marxist view of nature, supporting technological innovation, training interdisciplinary talent, and serving as a tool of practical critique for technology ethics and AI governance. Liu concludes that the manuscript, written in nineteenth-century Europe and still unfolding across three centuries, is steadily completing its "unfinished" mission. The article links the work to green development, ecological civilisation, high-quality development and new quality productive forces. Read the original if you want a concise account of how Dialectics of Nature was published and taught in China, and how a Chinese philosopher of science presents its present uses.

Striving unremittingly to advance national defence and military modernization with high quality Studying in depth Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China 为高质量推进国防和军队现代化不懈奋斗 Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Strengthening the Military This commentary, published in Guangming Daily on 29 December 2025, is a study guide to Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. They describe the plan as a blueprint for the next 20 to 30 years. The spirit and practical character of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era Studying Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China in depth 新时代全面深化改革的精神特质和实践品格 Office of the Commission for Deepening Overall Reform of the CPC Central Committee This study-guide article, published in the People's Daily by the office serving the Central Commission for Comprehensively Deepening Reform, reads the reform material in Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China together with Volumes I–IV. Advancing education, science and technology, and talent development as one: accelerating high-level scientific and technological self-reliance Studying in depth Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China 一体推进教育科技人才发展 加快实现高水平科技自立自强 Party Leadership Group of the Ministry of Science and Technology This study-and-implementation article, written by the Party leadership group of the Ministry of Science and Technology, takes up the chapter on advancing education, science and technology, and talent as one whole in Volume V of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Studying and implementing General Secretary Xi Jinping's important thinking on the Party's self-reform Studying volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China 深入学习贯彻习近平总书记关于党的自我革命的重要思想 Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and National Supervisory Commission This People's Daily article, written in the name of the Party's top discipline and supervision organs, is a study piece on volume five of Xi Jinping: The Governance of China. Continuously consolidating cultural subjectivity through the Two Integrations 在“两个结合”中不断巩固文化主体性 Hou Yanshe Hou Yanshe asks how the Two Integrations help consolidate the cultural subjectivity of the Chinese nation, meaning the autonomy, initiative and creativity that a historical subject shows in cultural activity. Scientific and technological innovation and science popularisation as the two wings of innovation-driven development 科技创新、科学普及是实现创新发展的两翼 Zhang Xiaofeng Qiao Xuezhu This commentary in Guangming Daily takes up Xi Jinping's formula that scientific and technological innovation and science popularisation are the "two wings" of innovation-driven development, and that popularisation should be given equal importance with innovation. The grand historical outlook of contemporary Chinese Communists 当代中国共产党人的大历史观 Huang Yibing Huang Yibing, a deputy director of the Central Institute of Party History and Literature, explains the "grand historical outlook" (da lishiguan) that Xi Jinping has advanced since the 18th Party Congress (2012). Adhering to integrated protection and systematic governance: building a protection and governance framework from mountain peak to ocean 坚持一体化保护和系统治理 构建从山顶到海洋的保护治理大格局 Zhang Bo This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 19 November 2025, asks how China should carry out integrated protection and systematic governance of mountains, rivers, forests, farmland, lakes, grassland and desert. Building an index of ideological and political guiding power: content system and scientific methods 构建思政引领力指数的内容体系与科学方法 Deng Zhe In 2024 Xi Jinping introduced the concept of "ideological and political guiding power" (sizheng yinlingli) at the National Education Conference and presented it as a distinctive feature of a strong education country with Chinese characteristics. This newspaper commentary asks how its level of development can be evaluated scientifically. Deng argues that an index should be constructed to assess regions and schools, analyse causes and optimise paths. The article sets out what the index should contain and how it should be built. It draws on the international "input–process–output" model of education indicators. It then covers the guiding principles of construction and four methodological innovations, with digital technology as a driver. Deng proposes a content system with three parts. The object system covers regions and schools, and within schools managers, educators and students at all stages. The link system covers ideological and political courses, ideology and politics across the curriculum, and everyday ideological work. The element system covers eight kinds of guidance, including ideological, political, cultural, value, belief, moral, emotional and action guidance. Construction should rest on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, existing evaluation standards, and paired principles such as combining quantitative and qualitative evaluation. Applied to the "Double First-Class" initiative, discipline assessment and education supervision, it would improve ideological and political work and help train a new generation to shoulder national rejuvenation. Read the original if you want a concise outline of how Chinese education scholars propose to measure ideological and political education.

Opening up a new path for humanity's march towards modernization 开辟人类迈向现代化的新道路 Zhang Guanzi This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in November 2025, asks what kind of modernization path is open to developing countries and what Chinese modernization offers them. The value of culture in empowering a new image for manufacturing, and ways to explore it 文化赋能制造业新形象的价值与探索 Huang Qi Gu Naihua This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 4 November 2025, asks how culture can help build a new image for Chinese manufacturing.
