The authors conclude that Chinese modernization has absorbed Chinese, socialist and other civilizational achievements, overcome the "civilizational barriers" set by Western modernization, and opened up a new picture of civilization. They add that this does not aim to replace "modernization equals Westernization" with "modernization equals Sinicization". In their account it shows that the human future has many possibilities and will be created by all humanity together. Read the original if you want to see how a Chinese Marxist journal grounds the claim of a new form of human civilization in classical-Marxist and Chinese cultural sources, and in a comparison with the West.

Understanding how to promote the intensive, quality-oriented development of university ideological and political courses through upholding fundamental principles and innovation 对守正创新推动高校思政课建设内涵式发展的领悟 Mei Rongzheng Mei Rongzheng takes up Xi Jinping's call, made at the 2019 teachers' symposium and repeated in instructions of May 2024, to promote the "connotative development" (内涵式发展, quality-oriented development) of ideological and political theory courses (sizheng ke) in schools. Mei argues that this is an important part of the connotative development of higher education as a whole and could push wider teaching reform further. Mei proposes five areas in which it can be achieved, guided by combining problem-orientation with goal-orientation and uniting upholding fundamental principles with innovation. The article first defines connotative development as growth driven by the internal essence and needs of a thing, as opposed to growth in scale. For the courses, this means that, once enrolment, staffing structure and funding are secured, teachers, curriculum and classroom teaching are to reform in concept, content, method, assessment, management, research and teacher quality. Mei then works through five points: one "fundamental" guide, one "key", one "focus", "three relationships" and one "historical summing-up". The fundamental is Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, which Mei says must run through every course and be taught with depth in its theory, reasoning and philosophy. The key is the teaching force. Mei says many newly hired teachers come from non-Marxist disciplines and are weak in Marxist theory, Party history and the Four-sphere Confidence, so leaders should track their circumstances and guide them. The focus is textbooks, where Mei asks whether the key textbooks of the Marxist Theory Research and Construction Project are really used and used well. On the three relationships, Mei argues that the Marxist theory discipline must serve the courses; that teachers should not be overloaded with outside tasks; and that new undergraduate majors must not drain core teachers. Mei also warns against returning to the earlier practice of spreading these courses across other departments. Mei reviews three curriculum schemes since reform and opening up (1985, 1998 and 2005) and says that a comprehensive, systematic assessment is needed of which experiences reflect teaching laws and which gaps remain. Mei proposes a large research group, led by the Ministry of Education's social sciences department, to produce a consultative report for decision-makers. Read the original if you want a Chinese academic's view of current staffing, textbook and institutional problems in university ideological and political courses and of the policy fixes he proposes.

Why does ideology "have no history"? The key problem in going beyond German idealism and the historical-materialist solution 意识形态何以“没有历史”？ Li Chengwang Li Chengwang asks how Marx and Engels were able to say, in The German Ideology, that morality, religion, metaphysics and other ideology have 'no history, no development'. The article argues that explaining this claim was the central task in surpassing German idealism and in establishing historical materialism. Li notes that research on the positive exposition of historical materialism is mature, whereas work on this particular problem remains comparatively thin. The article has three parts. The first traces Western philosophy's 'two-world' substance thinking from ancient Greece through medieval Christianity to Vico, Voltaire, Kant, Hegel and the Young Hegelians (Bruno Bauer, Feuerbach, Stirner). The second reconstructs the mechanism of material production in The German Ideology. The third follows Marx and Engels in showing historically how law, the state, religion, philosophy and morality depend on social relations, drawing on Engels's Ludwig Feuerbach and the End of Classical German Philosophy. Li contends that German idealism, despite internal differences, turns human history into a history of thought in which ideas, concepts or self-consciousness govern reality. Marx and Engels, in Li's account, begin instead from the empirical premise of producing the means of life and analyse production in five dimensions: the means of subsistence, new needs, human reproduction, the production of social relations, and the production of consciousness. Consciousness is therefore determined by production and the division of labour. Li then argues that Marx and Engels show, case by case, that ruling ideas express ruling material relations, that religious change follows economic needs, that Kantian and Feuerbachian ethics reflect bourgeois conditions, and that law and the state follow forms of ownership. Ideology thus has no independent history of its own. Li concludes that ideology is an inverted and illusory reflection of reality which cannot resolve real contradictions, and that its content changes with relations of production. Human history is a history of production and labour, and freedom is to be achieved through changing ownership and through communist revolution rather than through a revolution in ideas. Li presents this as the reason that historical materialism ends the idea that thought governs history. Read the original if you want a close reading of The German Ideology and Engels's Feuerbach essay as a systematic critique of German idealism.

The dialectical connections among the outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization 中华文明突出特性的辩证关联 Liu Zhihong Liu Zhihong takes up Xi Jinping's speech at the symposium on cultural inheritance and development, which identified five outstanding characteristics of Chinese civilization (continuity, innovation, unity, inclusiveness and peacefulness) and also discussed how they relate. The article, a commentary in Guangming Daily (2 October 2024), argues that each characteristic has its own irreplaceable value and that the five are organically linked. Liu holds that understanding their mutual reinforcement helps in grasping the overall nature of Chinese civilization and the scientific requirements of the Two Integrations. The piece has three parts. The first sets out the significance of each characteristic in turn, drawing heavily on Xi's formulations. The second shows how each characteristic supports every other. The third singles out several pairings that Liu treats as the key mechanisms of mutual reinforcement. Liu assigns each characteristic a distinct role. Continuity is the precondition, since without it the other four would have no ground. Innovation supplies inexhaustible force. Unity is the "main axis". Inclusiveness is the safeguard, and peacefulness is both a common result and a common guarantee of the others. On the key interactions, the author argues that unity and continuity are two sides of one thing, so that Chinese civilization has a continuous unity and a unified continuity. Inclusiveness and peacefulness are said to condition each other, and inclusiveness and innovation to generate each other. Unity and continuity are presented as conditions for inclusiveness, which in turn strengthens them. Liu adds that continuity is not stagnation but a historical process of progress supported by innovation. Liu concludes that the five characteristics form a dialectical unity that drives the development of Chinese civilization. The article follows the official line and offers no critique. It restates and systematises Xi's account instead. Read the original if you want a concise exposition of how current Party-aligned scholarship reads the relations among the five characteristics, as part of the discourse on the Two Integrations.

Two dimensions of the fusion of horizons between Marxism and biopolitics 马克思主义与生命政治学视域融合的两个维度 Lin Qing Why can Marxism and biopolitics (the study of how power takes human life and populations as its object) be brought into a shared horizon? In this short piece, first published in China Social Sciences Today in September 2024, Lin Qing argues that the two share an underlying logic: both centre on the capitalist mode of production and the governmentality it requires. The article is organised around two dimensions. The first concerns how the internal requirements of capitalist production, in particular the shift from absolute to relative surplus value, produce a politicisation of life. The second concerns the 'materiality' of power, drawing on Michel Foucault's reading of Marx. On the first dimension, Lin notes that Foucault ties biopolitics to liberalism, but holds that its original context lies in capitalist production. Absolute surplus value, obtained by lengthening the working day, meets natural limits of the body. Relative surplus value therefore requires care for population and labour-power, including raising workers' quality, and Lin cites Marx's remark that the state must legislate to force basic sanitation on capitalism. For Lin, Capital does not treat this theme explicitly but supplies the premise for understanding biopolitics. On the second dimension, Foucault criticises analyses that locate power in the state apparatus and ideology as 'Rousseauising' Marx, and Lin links this to Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme. Foucault finds in Capital four features of power: plural, not derived from sovereignty, productive rather than prohibitive, and technical, as in the factory. Lin concludes that biopolitics cannot be understood from its own concepts alone, and that changes in the capitalist mode of production explain its emergence. Power's materialism, in Foucault's reading of Marx, lies in concrete sites such as the factory rather than the state apparatus. Read the original if you want a brief account of how a Chinese scholar connects Foucault's biopolitics to Marx's analysis of relative surplus value and factory power.

A dialectical view of the relationship between Marx's philosophy and biopolitics 辩证地看待马克思哲学与生命政治学的关系 Wang Haifeng As biopolitics has become a popular topic in Chinese scholarship on Western left theory, this short commentary (first published in China Social Sciences Today, 2024) asks how it relates to Marx's philosophy. Wang Haifeng argues that the relation should be seen dialectically, by comparing the two in theme, content and orientation. In Wang's view, biopolitics continues Marx's critique of capitalism but takes a different path and offers a different solution. The article is organised in three steps, each matching one point of comparison: the shared theme of capitalist critique, the different understanding of "life", and the proposed routes to human emancipation. It draws mainly on Foucault, Hardt, Negri, Agamben and Esposito for biopolitics, and on Marx's 1844 Manuscripts, The German Ideology and Capital. Wang holds that, following Althusser's idea of a "problematic", biopolitics shares Marx's underlying problem even though its authors rarely cite him. It extends critique to micro-level power over populations, health and birth rates beyond the factory. For Marx, by contrast, life is always social and historical, tied to wage labour, surplus value and the logic of capital. This leads to different solutions. Agamben looks to a messianic "remnant" and Negri to irreducible singularity, whereas Marx locates the root of power over life in capital and calls for overturning capitalist social relations in favour of communism. Wang concludes that biopolitics widens the critical path Marx opened and enriches world Marxist theory. The article adds that the issues, resources and methods of Western Marxism offer lessons for building a contemporary Chinese Marxist philosophy able to address problems of Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a brief Chinese Marxist assessment of how biopolitics is positioned against Marx.

Extending and exceeding: biopolitics and political philosophy 拓展与跃出：生命政治学与政治哲学 Zheng Yuchen Zheng Yuchen asks how biopolitics, the field Michel Foucault developed, relates to political philosophy, a question on which scholars disagree. Citing Roberto Esposito, Zheng notes that Foucault's work shifted the whole framework of political philosophy. The article argues that biopolitics extends the classical framework and in part exceeds it. This newspaper essay appeared in 2024. The piece has three parts. It first outlines biopolitics' micro and macro dimensions and the debate over its status. It then compares the basic questions of biopolitics and political philosophy, and ends by assessing biopolitics' philosophical significance. Thinkers discussed include Foucault, Antonio Negri, Michael Hardt, Giorgio Agamben, Jacques Rancière and Esposito. Zheng argues that Anglo-American and continental political philosophy share one basic question, what a good common life is, but stress different mechanisms: coordination (rights, justice) versus coercion (sovereignty, the state of exception). With capitalism, the economy became central to politics, turning politics into biopolitics. Zheng contends that biopolitics finds hidden coercion inside liberalism's soft coordinating mechanisms, which are guaranteed by a sovereign 'night-watchman' able to declare exceptions. Biopolitics therefore belongs to the continental tradition. Its micro dimension carries power analysis into non-political fields such as medicine, culture and technology. Zheng concludes that the macro dimension joins classical debates by deconstructing them. The micro dimension leans towards social theory, and whether it counts as political philosophy remains contested and unresolved. Read the original if you want a compact Chinese-language map of how biopolitics is positioned against political philosophy, including the positions of Chinese scholars such as Lan Jiang and Xia Ying.

Further comprehensively deepening reform must adhere to a people-centred approach 进一步全面深化改革必须坚持以人民为中心 Huang Rongsheng Writing in Guangming Daily in September 2024, Huang Rongsheng takes up one of the principles set out in the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further comprehensively deepening reform: adhering to a people-centred approach. Huang argues that this principle expresses the Party's founding mission, the meaning of the phrase "Chinese modernization puts people's wellbeing first", and the value orientation of the new round of reform. The commentary is organised in three parts. The first traces the people-centred stance to Marxism's understanding of the people. The second links it to Chinese modernization and presents statistics on living standards. The third treats the people as the driving force of reform. Huang first argues that the people-centred approach inherits and develops the Marxist view that the masses make history. It cites Marx, Engels and Lenin, and then Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping and Xi Jinping. In this account the people's standpoint distinguishes Marxist parties from others, and the Party's growth from a small group into a major governing party results from adherence to it. Huang then contrasts Chinese modernization with what the article calls capital-centred Western modernization. As evidence of delivery, the article cites rising per capita disposable income (39,200 yuan in 2023), basic pension coverage above 1 billion people, basic medical insurance above 1.3 billion, and a public sense of security of 98.2%. Finally, Huang holds that more than four decades of reform show the people to be its fundamental driving force, citing poverty alleviation and the building of a moderately prosperous society. Huang concludes that reform must be carried out for the people and relying on them, with improving living standards as a key goal. The author calls for the Party's mass line to be followed in the new era, for top-level design to be combined with seeking the people's views, and for popular initiative to be mobilised. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the Party's official discourse links Marxist people-centred theory to the justification of current reform.

Further deepening reform comprehensively demonstrates historical initiative 进一步全面深化改革彰显历史主动 Wei Zhiqi This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 8 August 2024, interprets the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Wei Zhiqi argues that the decision shows the Party's "historical initiative" (lishi zhudong) in improving socialism with Chinese characteristics and modernizing national governance. The author opens by presenting reform and opening up as the key to Chinese modernization and credits it for the achievements since the 18th Party Congress (2012). The commentary then reads the Plenum through four themes, each framed by the word "historical": resolve, position, responsibility and confidence. On resolve, Wei cites Xi Jinping's insistence that Party leadership, Marxism, the socialist path and the people's democratic dictatorship cannot be shaken, and argues that this firmness lets the Party resist erroneous currents. On position, the author holds that China has moved from high-speed growth to high-quality development, with problems such as weak innovation, regional and income gaps, and that institution-building now carries greater weight. On responsibility, Wei describes reform as the self-improvement of the socialist system, with the Third Plenums of 2013 and 2024 forming a continuous logic that increasingly stresses systemic and coordinated reform. On confidence, Wei contends that opening up is a defining mark of Chinese modernization, that globalization remains the long-term trend, and that China should oppose deglobalization and protectionism. The author concludes that further reform will offer the world more opportunities and contribute to a community with a shared future for mankind. Read the original if you want a concise example of how the official press framed the 2024 Plenum's reform agenda.

Deepening reform along the track of the rule of law 坚持在法治轨道上深化改革 Zhai Guoqiang Writing in Economic Daily in August 2024, Zhai Guoqiang takes up the Decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which makes law-based governance a major principle of further deepening reform. Zhai's thesis is that reform and the rule of law must be unified, like two wings of a bird, and that the rule of law is both a component and a safeguard of Chinese modernization. The commentary has three sections. The first reviews how comprehensive law-based governance has taken shape since reform and opening up and under Xi Jinping. The second argues for the guiding, regulating and safeguarding role of law. The third sets out how to advance reform under law and improve law through reform. Zhai's core argument draws on comparison. In the author's account, every country that has modernized successfully has handled the problem of rule by law versus rule by individuals, while states that fell into development "traps" largely suffered from weak rule of law. On the reform–law relationship, Zhai holds that major reforms need a legal basis, but existing law must not become an excuse for delay. Mature experience should be quickly written into law, pilot reforms should be authorised by statutory procedure, and outdated provisions should be amended or repealed. Zhai names the building of a socialist rule-of-law system with Chinese characteristics as the overall lever. Zhai concludes that reform must uphold the unity of Party leadership, the people as masters of the country and law-based governance. The author also calls for implementing the Constitution and for fair enforcement, so that society stays both dynamic and orderly. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of how the 2024 Plenum links legal reform to Chinese modernization.

Relationships to handle well in safeguarding and improving people's livelihood through development 在发展中保障和改善民生需处理好若干关系 Lin Nan Wang Liexuan Published in Guangming Daily on 19 September 2024, this commentary by Lin Nan and Wang Liexuan takes up the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). The Decision describes safeguarding and improving people's livelihood through development as a major task of Chinese modernization, to be pursued by doing one's best while acting within one's means. The authors argue that carrying out this task requires handling several paired relationships correctly. The article takes six pairs in turn: top-level design and practical exploration; government leadership and multiple forces; economic development and improving livelihood; the present and the long term; overall advancement and breakthroughs in key areas; and doing one's best and acting within one's means. Each section sets out the two sides as complementary and then gives examples, mostly from social security, charity, employment, population policy, health reform and elderly care. Lin and Wang treat each pair as a dialectical unity rather than a choice. On the economy, they hold that growth is the material basis of better livelihood, and that livelihood work in turn drives high-quality development and opens new growth points. They cite figures: per capita disposable income rising from 16,510 yuan in 2012 to 39,218 yuan in 2023, basic pension coverage of nearly 1.1 billion people, and centralised drug procurement savings of about 300 billion yuan. On the last pair, they present doing one's best as the Party and government's responsibility, and acting within one's means as the requirement to base welfare on sustainable economic and fiscal capacity, so as to avoid a "high-welfare trap". The authors conclude that grasping these relationships, which they describe as a method of thinking and working stressed by Xi Jinping, will let policy combine firm direction with local initiative, state action with social participation, and urgent needs with lasting institutions. They say this will gradually bring about common prosperity for all. Read the original if you want a compact example of how official commentary translates the Third Plenum's livelihood language into working principles, with the statistics it uses.

Grasping the strategic priorities for advancing Chinese modernization 深刻把握推进中国式现代化的战略重点 Wu Yijun Zhao Yang This commentary, first published in Guangming Daily on 20 September 2024, reads the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Wu and Zhao argue that the decision's "seven focuses" together cover the strategic priorities of Chinese modernization. In their account, deepening reform in the new journey depends on grasping these priorities, ordering reform measures sensibly and carrying out the tasks effectively. The article takes the seven focuses in turn, giving each a short paragraph. They are: a high-standard socialist market economy; whole-process people's democracy; a socialist cultural powerhouse; a higher quality of life for the people; a beautiful China; a higher-level safe China; and better Party leadership and long-term governing capacity. Each section opens by placing the priority within Chinese modernization, cites Xi Jinping, summarises developments since the 18th Party Congress (2012) and ends with what is required in the new journey. The core of the argument is that each priority is both a component and a condition of Chinese modernization. The authors describe the socialist market economy as a creative combination of Marxist principles with practice, which can liberate and develop the productive forces and supply the material basis. Whole-process people's democracy is presented as an essential requirement of Chinese modernization, and the pursuit of common prosperity and a better life as its value goal. Ecological civilization, security and culture are treated as supporting foundations and spiritual underpinning. Party leadership, which the authors call the "most essential feature" of socialism with Chinese characteristics, is named the fundamental guarantee, and they link it to full and rigorous self-governance of the Party and the Party's self-reform. Wu and Zhao conclude that only by deepening reform along these seven lines can the goals of building a strong country and achieving the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation be realised. Throughout, they treat the achievements since 2012 as proof that the chosen path works. Read the original if you want a concise, official-style overview of how the Third Plenum's reform decision was framed for a general readership in 2024.

The construction logic of a high-standard socialist market economy 高水平社会主义市场经济体制的建构逻辑 Wang Shengsheng Following the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called a high-standard socialist market economy an important safeguard of Chinese modernization, Wang Shengsheng asks how such a system should be constructed. Writing in Guangming Daily on 24 September 2024, Wang argues that it bears on the whole of high-quality development and must be grasped through systems thinking. In this reading, its practical core is the dialectical unity of productive forces and relations of production, economic base and superstructure, and social development and state governance. The article is organised into four sections, each naming a requirement for building the system: upholding the Party's overall leadership; letting an effective market play its role; letting a capable government play its role; and building the system on a rule-of-law footing. Each section ends in concrete reform measures drawn from the Plenum's language, such as a unified national market, property-rights protection and institutional opening up. Wang's core claim is that the word "socialist" must be stressed first. Party leadership of economic work, in this account, secures the socialist direction of reform, mobilises the people and combines social mobilisation with organisational capacity, which Wang presents as a unity of democracy and centralism. An effective market depends on responsive price, supply-and-demand and competition mechanisms, on better division of labour and productivity through new quality productive forces, and on the Two Unwaverings, which Wang says free up market actors. A capable government is required because the law of value works spontaneously and the market cannot by itself settle accumulation and consumption, urban and rural areas, or regional layout. Wang gives government a role in organising major scientific projects, coordinating macroeconomic policy and building a new open economy with secure supply chains. Wang concludes that the system should be built in step with legal construction, with major reforms grounded in law and reform results codified. Constitutional authority, equal legal protection for all forms of ownership, competition and anti-monopoly rules, a Financial Law and alignment with high-standard international economic and trade rules are the measures proposed. Read the original if you want a concise statement of how official commentary after the 2024 Third Plenum links Party leadership, market, government and law in one framework.

Upholding a systems approach to further deepen reform comprehensively 坚持系统观念进一步全面深化改革 Ji Zhengju Wang Xiaorui This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 13 August 2024, takes up how reform should be advanced after the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Ji and Wang argue that the systems approach (xitong guannian) is both a valuable lesson of comprehensively deepening reform in the new era and a major principle that further reform must follow. The piece has three parts. It first traces the systems approach through successive Party leaderships, from Deng Xiaoping to Xi Jinping. It then discusses five major relationships that reform must handle: economy and society, government and market, efficiency and fairness, vitality and order, and development and security. It closes with three practical requirements for putting the approach into effect. On the first part, the authors present the systems approach as a methodological summary of reform practice since reform and opening up. They cite Deng's view of reform as comprehensive, Jiang Zemin's twelve major relationships and Hu Jintao's "ten combinations", and argue that under Xi Jinping reform moved from local experiments and breakthroughs to systems integration. On the second, they hold that each pair of relationships is mutually reinforcing rather than opposed. Examples include the government and the market working as "two hands", fairness not meaning egalitarianism ("first make the cake bigger"), and high-quality development and high-level security supporting each other. The authors call for stronger systems integration, with the Party exercising overall leadership, top-level design and coordination, and breakthroughs at key points driving the whole. They call for overall advancement, in which local and overall interests, root causes and symptoms, and gradual and breakthrough measures are combined. They also call for more coordinated reforms across fields from the market economy and whole-process people's democracy to ecological civilisation and national defence, backed by strong coordination mechanisms and supervision to ensure implementation. Read the original if you want a concise official-style statement of how the systems approach is meant to guide the reform agenda adopted in 2024.

Comrade Deng Xiaoping's strategic blueprint for China's modernization drive 邓小平同志对中国现代化建设的战略擘画 Wang Tao Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts in 2024, Wang Tao takes up Xi Jinping's description of Deng Xiaoping as chief architect of reform and opening up and of socialist modernization. The article asks how Deng's strategic thinking shaped China's modernization. It argues that Deng drew up a coherent blueprint whose parts were seizing opportunity, defining tasks, setting requirements, fixing stages and shaping the strategic environment, and that this blueprint is now being turned into reality. The commentary is organised in five sections: perceiving strategic opportunity, clarifying strategic tasks, setting strategic requirements, defining strategic stages, and shaping the strategic environment. Wang relies mainly on Deng's own remarks, from his 1978 Japan visit and the 1980s talks with foreign guests to his 1990s comments to Party leaders and his southern tour speeches. The text opens with Xi Jinping's speech marking the 120th anniversary of Deng's birth and closes by linking Deng's legacy to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). Wang's central claim is that Deng combined urgency with realism. On opportunity, Deng saw peace and development as the two main themes of the era and repeatedly warned against losing the chance to develop, including after the sanctions of 1989–90. On tasks, he inherited the 'four modernizations' and redefined the goal as a modest 'moderately prosperous society', treating economic construction as the centre and the liberation and development of the productive forces as the essence of socialism. His 'three-step' strategy, written into the 13th Party Congress report (1987), rested on the judgement that China was in the primary stage of socialism and set a path to mid-level developed status by the middle of the 21st century. Wang adds that Deng required adherence to the Four Cardinal Principles, Party leadership and 'bold experimentation' only with matters 'clearly seen', with stability and a peaceful external setting as preconditions. Wang concludes that Deng's restraint, patience and firm faith in socialism are a lasting political lesson. The article ties this to Xi's call to carry forward socialism with Chinese characteristics, noting that only a little over ten years remain to the goal of basically realizing modernization and a little over twenty to the goal of a modern socialist power. Read the original if you want a concise Party-press synthesis of Deng's quoted statements on modernization strategy and of how they are linked to current policy.

"Act in accordance with dialectics": Deng Xiaoping's far-sighted strategic thinking “照辩证法办事”：邓小平同志高瞻远瞩的战略思维 Li Qinggang Li Qinggang takes up the strategic thinking that Xi Jinping, at the symposium marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, listed among Deng's defining qualities. The article, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, argues that this thinking rests on a Marxist philosophical foundation summed up in Deng's phrase "act in accordance with dialectics" (zhao bianzhengfa banshi), a phrase Mao Zedong endorsed in 1945 and again in 1957 when urging the whole Party to study dialectics. Li organises the discussion into five paired principles, each illustrated with examples from Deng's wartime, early-PRC and reform-era work. These are: holding firmly to the principal contradiction; combining the doctrine of emphasis on the key point with the doctrine of two sides; subordinating the small picture to the big picture; seizing opportunities and deciding in time; and being bold while taking steady steps. In Li's account, Deng's wartime insistence on widening the Sino-Japanese contradiction and his post-1978 insistence on making economic development the centre of Party work both show him grasping the principal contradiction and refusing to let go. Li reads "grasp with both hands, and both must be firm" (material and cultural-ethical progress, construction and legal order, development and stability) as the unity of emphasis and balance. Li cites Deng's remarks on coastal and inland development, and the Huaihai campaign decision, as cases of putting the overall situation first. Li also treats "crossing the river by feeling the stones" and the push for faster growth in the 1992 southern tour as timing guided by the move from quantitative to qualitative change. "Bold in spirit, steady in step" is presented as uniting subjective initiative with respect for objective laws. Li concludes that the founding of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the achievements of reform and opening up cannot be separated from Deng's strategic thinking and Deng Xiaoping Theory. Quoting Xi, Li says the theory must be grasped in its historical context and as a whole, since one-sided reading risks errors of principle and direction. Li calls on Party members and cadres to learn Deng's global and long-term outlook and his method of seizing the key link, so as to advance the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. Read the original if you want a concise, officially framed account of how Deng's pragmatic sayings are presented as applications of materialist dialectics.

Deng Xiaoping's reform thought and its value for our times 邓小平改革思想及其时代价值 Qu Qingshan Qu Qingshan's article, published in Qiushi in 2024 and framed by Xi Jinping's speech marking the 120th anniversary of Deng Xiaoping's birth, asks what Deng's thinking on reform consisted of and why it still matters. Qu argues that Deng, as chief architect of reform and opening up, produced a complete system of thought on reform, an important component of Deng Xiaoping Theory. In Qu's reading, it remains a guide for further comprehensively deepening reform and for advancing Chinese modernization. The article has three parts. The first sets out the historical conditions in which Deng's reform thought arose, summarised as four 'groundings'. The second lists the content of that thought under eight headings, and notes the results of reform and opening up. The third links Deng's ideas to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and to its 'six adherences' as principles for further reform. Qu says the four groundings were an understanding of the Party's and the country's fate at the end of the Cultural Revolution, a review of socialist experience at home and abroad, a reading of world trends, and attention to the people's aspirations. The eight themes are Party leadership, reliance on the masses, reform as the self-improvement of the socialist system, reform as liberating the productive forces, comprehensive reform, boldness combined with steady steps, the 'three favourables' as criteria, and opening up as part of reform. Qu then pairs each of the six principles of the 2024 Plenum with Deng's ideas: Party leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while innovating, institution-building, rule of law, and systems thinking. Qu concludes that reform and opening up has transformed China, citing the shift from a planned to a socialist market economy and an economy that became the world's second largest. The article describes this as vindicating Deng's decision and as the necessary road to national rejuvenation. It calls for continued reform under the Central Committee with Xi Jinping at its core. Read the original if you want an official Party-journal account of how Deng's reform thought is being linked to the current reform agenda and to the 2024 Plenum.

Exploring paths to accelerate the development of new quality productive forces 探索加快发展新质生产力的路径 Yu Li This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in July 2024, asks how new quality productive forces can be developed faster. Yu argues that Xi Jinping's statements on the subject carry major theoretical and practical significance. The article holds that deepening understanding of them and finding concrete paths will support high-quality development and bring strategic initiative in international competition. The piece is organised around four paths: developing new quality productive forces according to local conditions, strengthening science and technology innovation, deepening institutional reform, and building a large pool of high-calibre talent. Each section opens with a quotation from Xi and then sets out policy recommendations. On local conditions, Yu calls for adherence to the Party's overall leadership and for each region to build on its own resources, avoiding blind imitation. On innovation, the author points to bottlenecks in core technologies and supply chains and to trade frictions created by some Western countries. Yu urges stronger basic research, upgrading of traditional industries and deeper integration of the digital and real economies. On reform, the author argues that production relations must suit the productive forces, and proposes a unified national market, an effective market working with an effective government, and wider opening up. On talent, Yu proposes expanded vocational education, more open recruitment and less burdensome evaluation for researchers. The article concludes that these four steps together would create conditions for new quality productive forces and strengthen the drivers of high-quality development. Read the original if you want a brief example of how official commentary translates Xi's remarks on new quality productive forces into a policy checklist.

Developing new quality productive forces requires winning five innovation campaigns 发展新质生产力亟待打好五大创新战役 Fan Jida Fan Jida asks how China should organise innovation in order to develop new quality productive forces, which the article defines as an advanced form of productive forces led by innovation, marked by high technology, high efficiency and high quality, and consistent with the new development philosophy. Fan argues that, in light of a new round of technological revolution and the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), the task should be pursued through five distinct "campaigns". The piece appeared in Red Flag Manuscript (Hongqi Wengao) in 2024 and cites Xi Jinping's statement that high-quality development requires such productive forces. The article is organised as five sections, each framed as a campaign: a decisive battle on key core technologies, a protracted war on basic research, a contest for innovative talent, a breakout battle for enterprises in competition, and a positional battle for regional innovation. Each section combines a diagnosis of current weaknesses with policy proposals, and cites the Third Plenum's wording. Fan draws on figures for research spending and on historical examples of Britain and Germany to support the case. On technology, Fan says many key technologies remain controlled by others and calls for strengthening national laboratories, the Chinese Academies of Sciences and Engineering, and research universities. The new-type whole-nation system, Fan stresses, is not government control of everything, a substitute for private-sector innovation, or a return to the planned economy. On basic research, Fan cites 2023 spending of 2,212 billion yuan, only 6.65 per cent of R&D funding, and argues that many bottleneck problems stem from weak foundational theory. Fan proposes steadier funding, more autonomy for scientists and new evaluation methods. On talent, enterprises and regions, Fan calls for reform of education, support for young scientists, immigration arrangements for high-tech talent, and enterprise R&D reserves and patient capital. Fan also proposes innovation centres in Beijing, Shanghai and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area, and upgrading traditional industries rather than abandoning them. Fan concludes that these five campaigns together form the path to developing new quality productive forces, and that matching production relations, meaning institutional and management reform, must accompany technological effort. The text also stresses openness, arguing that regions should use international innovation resources rather than pursue self-isolation. Read the original if you want a Party-journal statement of how the Third Plenum's innovation agenda is translated into specific policy priorities on science funding, talent, enterprises and regional development.

New quality productive forces inject momentum into high-quality development 新质生产力为高质量发展注入动能 Yuan Lei This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 23 July 2024, takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) and its call to treat high-quality development as the primary task of building a modern socialist country. Yuan Lei argues that new quality productive forces are an inherent requirement of high-quality development and a key lever for it. The author presents the concept as Xi Jinping's theoretical summary of productive-force development in the new era, drawing on the basic principles of Marxist political economy. The article is organised in three parts. The first explains why developing new quality productive forces follows from the new development stage, the new development philosophy and the new development pattern. The second sets out four "dividends" through which they are said to raise total factor productivity. The third lists four routes to high-level scientific and technological self-reliance. Yuan's central claim is that new quality productive forces raise total factor productivity, which the author calls the key to improving both the quality and the quantity of growth. The four dividends are technological (new products and higher efficiency, with traditional industries said to make up over 80% of manufacturing), structural (innovative allocation of production factors as the old shift from agriculture to manufacturing slows), green (the author cites energy use per unit of GDP at about 1.5 times the world average, and an output target of 11 trillion yuan for green industries by 2025) and reform-related. The reform dividend is tied to changes in the relations of production: reform of the economic system, the science and technology system, factor markets and income distribution. Yuan also argues that these forces can ease regional imbalances, cut resource costs, support opening up and help domestic and international circulation. Yuan proposes four tasks: let scientific and technological innovation lead, especially in basic research; push industrial upgrading through strategic emerging and future industries; accelerate the green transformation of development; and build institutions that let each region develop new quality productive forces according to local conditions. The author presents these as the way to secure a material and technological base for Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official economic commentary links new quality productive forces to total factor productivity and institutional reform.

The theoretical connotations and practical requirements of new quality productive forces 新质生产力的理论内涵和实践要求 Xu Jianwei Li Ziwen This newspaper commentary, published in Economic Daily in July 2024, asks what new quality productive forces are and how they should be developed. Xu Jianwei and Li Ziwen present Xi Jinping's statements on the subject as an innovation and development of the Marxist theory of productive forces. They argue that the theoretical meaning of the concept must be combined with concrete practical requirements. The article first sets out the content of the concept, then turns to six practical requirements. It treats the new development philosophy, scientific and technological innovation, the optimal recombination of production factors, the modern industrial system, total factor productivity and deepened reform as the guiding principle, driver, substance, carrier, marker and safeguard of the new productive forces. On the theory, the authors define new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces in line with the new development philosophy. Their basic content is a leap in workers, means of labour, objects of labour and their optimal combination, and they form an organic whole. Technological innovation is the core factor, the modern industrial system is the carrier, and a large rise in total factor productivity is the core marker. Supply-chain resilience and lower emissions are further measures. On practice, the authors distinguish two kinds of innovation: broadly penetrating technological revolutions and vertically disruptive technological changes. They say weak traditional industries reflect insufficient innovation, and they call for innovation to be applied to upgrading traditional industries, nurturing emerging ones and planning future ones. The authors conclude that relations of production must suit the development of productive forces, so further comprehensive deepening of reform is needed to build new-type production relations. They call for reforms in science, education and talent systems, factor markets, opening up and income distribution. Read the original if you want a concise official-style summary of how the new quality productive forces concept was framed in Chinese policy discussion in mid-2024.

Making better use of market mechanisms and creating a fairer, more dynamic market environment 更好发挥市场机制作用 创造更加公平、更有活力的市场环境 Luo Wen Writing in Qiushi (2024, no. 17), Luo Wen interprets the market-related sections of the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The article takes up the core question of the government–market relationship and argues that market regulators must raise their comprehensive supervisory capacity so that the market is both free enough ("放得活", "let go effectively") and well enough governed ("管得住", "kept under control"). In Luo's account, this serves to optimise resource allocation, remedy market failure and release innovation. The piece is a policy commentary organised in six parts, each linking a passage of the Decision to the tasks of market supervision. They cover basic market-economy institutions, the healthy development of business entities, fair competition policy, market order, public-safety baselines, and the modernization of comprehensive market supervision. Each part first explains why the Decision's provision matters, then lists concrete measures for the regulatory authorities. Luo's central claim is that vitality and order are organically unified, which the article equates with a better combination of an efficient market and a capable government. On one side, it calls for protecting property rights, market access, credit systems and equal treatment of all forms of ownership under the Two Unwaverings, while curbing local protectionism, market fragmentation, monopoly and unfair competition. On the other, it holds that price violations, counterfeits and false advertising distort incentives, and that food, drug and industrial safety are expressions of market failure that the state must address. For supervision itself, Luo proposes tools including graded credit regulation, unified information systems, "smart supervision" and standardised administrative discretion. The article calls for strengthening legal, credit-based and smart supervision to fit a super-large market, and presents this as support for modernising national governance. Specific measures include a mandatory exit system for business entities, trade-secret protection, a review system for fair competition, regulation of platform firms and stronger consumer-rights enforcement. Read the original if you want a detailed, official-line account of how China's market regulators translate the Third Plenum Decision into concrete supervisory tasks.

The contemporary expression of building an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences 构建中国哲学社会科学自主知识体系的时代表达 Lü Xinbin Writing in the Chinese Social Sciences Today in September 2024, Lü Xinbin takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which named the building of an independent knowledge system of Chinese philosophy and social sciences as a strategic task. Lü argues that, if reform is to power this task, it must rest on three underlying logics: a fundamental direction, a fundamental attitude and a fundamental path. The commentary is organised under three headings: "holding to the soul and the roots" (direction), "firm confidence and consciousness" (attitude), and "adhering to innovation and creation" (path). Each section draws on Xi Jinping's statements and on the 20th Party Congress (2022) and Third Plenum documents. Lü also gives examples from the Hebei Academy of Social Sciences, which Lü presents as putting each principle into practice through research projects and reform programmes. On direction, Lü holds that the "soul" is Marxism, now embodied in Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and Xi Jinping's thought on culture, and the "roots" are fine traditional Chinese culture. The two are joined in the Two Integrations and in the practice of Chinese modernization. On attitude, Lü calls for cultural subjectivity, intellectual independence and a sense of mission, and says China is creating a new form of human civilisation that goes beyond Western capitalist and traditional socialist civilisations, in which Chinese social science should play a foundational and leading role. On path, Lü stresses innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture, plus creative transformation and innovative development of tradition. Lü argues that no ready-made textbook exists for China's social transformation, so new concepts and categories must be drawn from Chinese practice. Lü concludes that direction settles the question of the banner of reform, attitude the question of resolve, and path the question of substance, and that together they will bring a new era of flourishing for the independent knowledge system. Lü expects theory to interpret Chinese practice and practice to enrich theory, and envisions a more systematic, scholarly Chinese social science. Read the original if you want a representative example of how official commentary after the Third Plenum frames the task of building an independent knowledge system, including local academy examples from Hebei.

Building a high-standard socialist market economy 构建高水平社会主义市场经济体制 Guo Chunli Guo Chunli takes up the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) formulation that a high-standard socialist market economy is an important guarantee for Chinese modernization. This newspaper commentary argues that the system should be built by improving four things: high-quality business entities, a high-standard market system, high-efficiency basic institutions of the market economy, and a high-efficiency governance system. Guo presents this as a way to supply strong momentum and institutional support for Chinese modernization. The piece has three parts. The first sets out why the system is needed and what it means, tracing the socialist market economy from the Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee through the 14th Party Congress and the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee to the 2024 plenum. The second lists four ways in which the system underpins Chinese modernization. The third sets out four practical tasks. In Guo's account, the core of the system is the "decisive role" of the market in allocating resources together with a better-performing government, producing what the article calls an effective market and a capable government in organic unity. The author reads the reform record as a deepening Party understanding of market laws and a search for an economic system suited to the productive forces, including new quality productive forces. The four guarantees are: meeting the goals for 2035 and the mid-century target, mainly by raising total factor productivity; applying the new development philosophy fully; building a new development pattern through a national unified market and domestic–international dual circulation; and promoting high-quality development. Guo's four tasks are to uphold the Two Unwaverings, including a law to promote the private economy, to build a unified national market, to improve basic market institutions (property rights, market access, bankruptcy, social credit), and to improve macroeconomic governance. The last covers policy coordination, fiscal, tax and financial reform, and regional coordination. The piece is an official-line statement of how the plenum's market-economy agenda is to be understood and implemented. Read the original if you want a concise, authoritative-style overview of the policy priorities and rationale for the "high-standard socialist market economy" after the 2024 plenum.

Finding the right path to accelerate the cultivation and development of new quality productive forces 找准路径加快培育发展新质生产力 Deng Quheng This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 29 August 2024, asks how China can speed up the cultivation of new quality productive forces. Deng Quheng argues that the path runs through three tasks: deep industrial transformation and upgrading, innovative allocation of production factors, and deeper reform of institutions and mechanisms. The piece takes its direction from the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which it quotes at the outset. The article is organised under three headings that match these tasks. The first deals with industrial structure, the balance between traditional, emerging and future industries, and coordination among regions. The second covers technology, talent and finance as the main factors to be allocated. The third turns to markets, income distribution, and the joint development of education, science and technology, and talent. Deng holds that upgrading industry raises labour productivity and total factor productivity and helps China gain the initiative in a restructuring of global industrial chains. Traditional industries, which the author says make up over 80% of manufacturing, should become carriers of new quality productive forces, while strategic emerging and future industries receive support for core technology breakthroughs. On factors, Deng calls for pooling scientific resources through the new whole-nation system, turning the demographic dividend into a talent dividend, and steering finance, including patient capital, towards early-stage and hard-technology projects. Citing the principle that production relations must suit the productive forces, the author proposes building new production relations by improving factor markets, relying on state-owned enterprises and private firms, and reforming income distribution. Deng concludes that reform must clear the blockages that hold back new quality productive forces and let advanced innovation factors gather around them. Education, science and technology, and talent cultivation are to be advanced together. Read the original if you want a concise policy-oriented overview of how a Chinese economist links the Third Plenum's reform agenda to new quality productive forces.

Upholding a systems approach in developing new quality productive forces 坚持系统观念发展新质生产力 Yang Yanlin Ge Xuanchang This short commentary, first published in Economic Daily in September 2024, asks how new quality productive forces should be developed. Yang and Ge argue that this is a systemic undertaking touching every area of economic and social life, and that it requires a systems approach. They tie the argument to the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024), which called for sound institutions for developing new quality productive forces in line with local conditions. The authors first define new quality productive forces and analyse them from the standpoint of systems theory. They then set out two methodological principles, and close with three practical measures: basic research, talent and the modern industrial system. In the authors' account, new quality productive forces are a complex system of elements, structure and function. The elements are new types of workers, objects of labour, instruments of labour and infrastructure; the structure is a modern industrial system led by emerging and future industries; the function is to raise total factor productivity and meet people's needs for a better life. They stress that these forces are a qualitative leap driven by innovation, not a marginal improvement on traditional productive forces. Two principles follow: proceed from local realities, since no uniform template exists, and advance as a whole while achieving breakthroughs at key points. The authors add that emerging industries and the digital, green and integrated upgrading of traditional industries should reinforce each other. Yang and Ge call for sustained investment in basic research and organised research, a strategy of strengthening the country through talent, with fewer barriers to mobility and a reformed evaluation system, and a modern industrial system with secure, self-controlled industrial and supply chains. They name quantum information, brain-inspired intelligence, gene technology and brain–computer interfaces as targets for breakthroughs. Read the original if you want a concise statement of the official systems-based reading of new quality productive forces and its policy priorities.

Paying attention to strengthening the Party's leadership over reform 注重加强党对改革的领导 Cao Wenze This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 22 August 2024, reads the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform and advancing Chinese modernization. Cao Wenze argues that Party leadership is the fundamental guarantee of further comprehensive deepening of reform, and that it must run through every aspect and stage of reform. The piece is organised in four short sections. It deals in turn with the Party's vanguard character as the reason for leading reform, the full leadership of the Party as an experience and principle of reform since 1978, the building of a stronger Marxist party, and the Party's self-reform as the guide of broader social revolution. Cao begins from the Communist Manifesto, taking Marx and Engels's account of communists as the most resolute, driving section of the movement to mean that a Marxist party is inherently reform-minded. The author then argues that reform has reached its "deepest part of the deep waters", where deep institutional problems rather than local ones are at stake. In this setting, Cao holds, the Party must uphold the Two Establishes and the Two Upholds so that reform avoids both a rigid closed path and a path of abandoning socialism. Cao also presents Party leadership and Party building as advancing together: reform requires full and rigorous self-governance of the Party, and better leadership is itself an internal requirement of reform. Cao concludes that the Party should strengthen centralised, unified leadership and the mechanisms for implementing Central Committee decisions, and should pursue the Party's self-reform through ideological, organisational, conduct and discipline building and anti-corruption work. The stated aim is to complete the Decision's reform tasks by 2029, the 80th anniversary of the People's Republic. Read the original if you want a concise example of how official commentary justifies Party leadership of reform after the Third Plenum.

Deepening reform to provide momentum for developing new quality productive forces 深化改革为发展新质生产力提供动力 Zhang Wanming Writing in Economic Daily on 28 August 2024, Zhang Wanming argues that speeding up new quality productive forces is a question of reform as much as of development. Taking the decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) as its starting point, the commentary holds that further comprehensively deepening reform is needed to build production relations better suited to these forces and to raise total factor productivity. The piece moves in three steps. It first sets out what developing new quality productive forces requires, then explains why reform must continue in three areas, and finally lists the institutional mechanisms to be improved. Zhang follows the Plenum's wording closely and presents the argument as an application of the Party's line. Zhang defines new quality productive forces as an advanced form of productive forces produced by revolutionary technological breakthroughs, innovative allocation of production factors and deep industrial transformation and upgrading. Three requirements follow: innovation as the primary driving force, a modern industrial system as the main lever, and efficient allocation of production factors as the foothold. Zhang then argues that reform is itself innovation, with technological and institutional innovation compared to a bird's two wings. Reform is said to be needed to release innovative vitality, to deepen industrial upgrading through supply-side structural reform, and to correct the misallocation of factors, including barriers to urban–rural exchange. Four sets of measures are proposed: reform of the science and technology system, reform of market-based allocation of factors (property protection, market access, fair competition, a unified national market, the Two Unwaverings), reform of talent development, and wider high-level opening up, including institutional opening up. Zhang concludes that new quality productive forces should be pursued through comprehensive reform of the economic, scientific, educational, talent and financial systems, and by improving mechanisms suited to local conditions. The commentary treats reform and opening up as the means of releasing productive potential. Read the original if you want a concise, officially aligned account of how reform is linked to new quality productive forces in the policy discussion after the Third Plenum.

Upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground to keep reform steady and far-reaching 坚持守正创新推动改革行稳致远 Zhang Hao This commentary in Economic Daily takes up one of the major principles of the decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024): "upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground" (守正创新). On the first side, Zhang argues that reform must keep to the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics, rejecting both a rigid, closed path and a path of changing banners. The author lists five anchors: the Four Cardinal Principles, Chinese modernization as the theme, the overall goal of improving the socialist system and modernizing national governance, and the socialist market economy. On the second side, Zhang calls for courage in emancipating the mind, a problem-oriented approach aimed at deep-seated institutional obstacles, and innovation in theory, practice, institutions and culture. Methodological features of further deepening reform comprehensively 进一步全面深化改革的方法论特征 Liu Mingsong This commentary, published in Guangming Daily in September 2024, interprets the methodology behind the Decision of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. The Decision calls for "paying more attention" to three things: systems integration, key priorities and practical results. Liu argues that these three emphases summarise the methodology of the reform effort so far and are the distinctive methodological features of the next stage. In Liu's view, only a scientific method can keep reform clear in direction and steady in progress, so that it supplies momentum and institutional guarantees for Chinese modernization. The article is organised in three sections, one for each "paying more attention". Each section gives a philosophical grounding, an assessment of the reform record since the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013), and a set of requirements for the new stage. It is a short official-style commentary rather than a research study, and it relies on Party documents and the vocabulary of materialist dialectics. On systems integration, Liu grounds the principle in the dialectical view of universal connection: society is an organic system whose elements constrain and affect one another. Reform has moved from laying foundations to comprehensive advance and now to integration and coordination. Because structural contradictions have sharpened, Liu holds, single-item or piecemeal reform no longer suffices. Reform must be made more systematic, integrated and coordinated, with economic reform leading and the Party's leadership as the coordinating core. On key priorities, Liu invokes the unity of the "two-point" and "key-point" approaches, meaning attention to principal versus secondary contradictions. Priorities include the government–market relationship, high-quality development, macroeconomic governance, urban–rural integration and high-level opening up, together with livelihood problems such as housing, employment and healthcare. On practical results, Liu stresses implementation: a plan means little unless it takes effect. The author calls for a "nail-driving spirit", a correct view of performance, avoidance of formalism and vanity projects, and better mechanisms for follow-up, supervision and evaluation. Liu concludes that Chinese modernization advances through reform and opening up, and that the Party must grasp these methodological features and turn the strategic plans of the Decision into driving force for modernization. The text offers a compact guide to how official commentary frames the method of the current reform agenda. Read the original if you want a concise example of how Chinese Party-affiliated writers link materialist dialectics to the policy method of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee.

Grasping the rich connotations and practical requirements of new quality productive forces 把握新质生产力的丰富内涵和实践要求 Zhong Ying Wang Lu This short commentary, first published in the People's Daily on 6 September 2024, asks how new quality productive forces should be understood and developed in light of the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024). On technology, the authors hold that scientific and technological innovation is the core element, producing new industries, models and drivers of growth, and they call for original and disruptive innovation and breakthroughs in key core technologies. On factors of production, they say the "newness" lies in new qualities of labourers, means of labour and objects of labour, and in their optimised recombination, which raises total factor productivity. On industry, they note that traditional industries make up over 80 per cent of manufacturing and should be upgraded with digital-intelligence and green technologies rather than phased out as "low-end"; strategic emerging and future industries are described as the main arena. Keeping institution-building as the main thread 始终突出制度建设这条主线 Tao Wenzhao This commentary, first published in Economic Daily on 22 August 2024, explains why the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) made "adhering to institution-building as the main thread" an important principle of further comprehensively deepening reform. In Tao's reading, this signals continuity and stages in the same effort. On history, Tao traces a path from Deng Xiaoping's remark on a more mature and fixed system, through the Third Plenum of the 18th Central Committee (2013) and the Fourth Plenum of the 19th Central Committee (2019), to a stage that demands more systematic and coordinated design. Read the original if you want a concise, official-line account of why institution-building is presented as the organising principle of the 2024 reform agenda.

Summing up and elevating the Party's successful experience in leading reform and opening up 党领导改革开放成功经验的总结升华 Jin Minqing This commentary, first published in Economic Daily in September 2024, reads the Decision of the Central Committee on further deepening reform comprehensively to advance Chinese modernization (the Third Plenum document of 2024) as a summing-up and elevation of the Party's successful experience. On the second, Jin presents the six principles as a scientific and complete whole: the Party's overall leadership, a people-centred approach, upholding fundamental principles while breaking new ground, institution building as the main thread, law-based governance, and systemic thinking. On the third, Jin lists the emphases as the leading role of economic reform, a system supporting all-round innovation, comprehensive reform, balancing development and security, and strengthening Party leadership of reform. Jin concludes that the five emphases reinforce one another and that breakthroughs in key areas will drive overall progress, turning the strategy of further deepening reform into strength for advancing Chinese modernization. Read the original if you want a concise official-line reading of how the Third Plenum Decision is framed as continuous with four decades of reform experience.

Grasping scientifically the major significance and practical requirements of deepening institutional reform in Party building 科学把握深化党的建设制度改革的重大意义和实践要求 Liu Zhiming This commentary, published in Red Flag Manuscript in 2024, interprets the part of the Decision adopted at the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) that deals with institutional reform in Party building. Liu argues that the Decision answers what to reform, how to reform and what results to seek in this field. In Liu's reading, the Decision sets out the fundamental guidance for strengthening the Party's leadership and its capacity for long-term governance under the overall goal of further comprehensively deepening reform. The article has three parts. The first explains why deepening Party-building reform matters. The second sets out the basic requirements for carrying it out. Liu gives three reasons for the significance of this reform. First, it is an integral part of modernizing the system and capacity of national governance, and it also guarantees that wider reform succeeds. Second, it is needed to mobilise Party members and officials to push reform and development, since deeper reform meets greater resistance. Third, it is required by the new great undertaking of Party building and by the need to deal with problems unique to a large party, such as slackness, incompetence, detachment from the people and corruption. On requirements, Liu calls for Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era as guidance. Liu also stresses three things that must not change: the Party's centralised and unified leadership of reform, the overall goal, and the people-centred value orientation. For implementation, Liu lists measures including the "first agenda item" system, the eight-point regulation, a correct view of performance, the "three distinctions", expanded Party coverage in new economic and social organisations, and an accountability system for implementing Party regulations. Liu concludes that Party-building reform is "always in progress, never finished" and that the Party's own strength is the key to Chinese modernization and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. The article is a programmatic reading of the Decision, written from within the Party-state academic system. Read the original if you want a concise official-style account of how Party-building reform is framed after the Third Plenum, and of the practical measures it names for cadres, grassroots organisations and Party regulations.

Party leadership as the fundamental guarantee for further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization 党的领导是进一步全面深化改革、推进中国式现代化的根本保证 Shi Yubao Writing in Red Flag Manuscripts (2024, no. 17), Shi Yubao interprets the Decision adopted by the Third Plenum of the 20th Central Committee (2024) on further deepening reform comprehensively and advancing Chinese modernization. Shi presents the Party's overall leadership as a basic principle of scientific socialism, as the most valuable experience of revolution, construction and reform, and as a necessity given external pressure and domestic structural problems. The article then maintains that reform must proceed under the Central Committee's unified leadership. On the institutional side, Shi proposes reforms in cadre personnel management, grassroots organisations, the education and management of Party members (cited as 99.185 million at the end of 2023) and talent development.
